sections.html:
Pierce County is a rural southeast Georgia county with Blackshear as its seat, set along the Alabaha River. The mid-2025 count is 20,764 people, up 5.3 percent from 2020, spread over 340.46 square miles of land. Only 68 building permits were issued in 2025, so a resale competes with little new housing.

The median owner-occupied value is $153,300 (2020 to 2024). About three homes in four (76.5 percent) are owner-occupied, and median rent is $799. With prices like these, unpaid tax can swallow a large part of the proceeds, so learn the balance early.

Storm damage can also affect a sale. Hurricane Debby damaged personal and business property in the county. A seller with a damaged roof or outbuilding should keep photographs and repair estimates, since a buyer's inspection will ask about them.

Duties divide between the Tax Commissioner and the Board of Assessors, whose offices are both on Nichols Street in Blackshear. The commissioner's office is independent of the assessors and of the county commissioners, who control only its budget. Its main duty is to collect the taxes the assessors set.

Pierce County tax offices in Blackshear
OfficeAddressPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner312 Nichols Street, Suite 4, Blackshear, GA 31516 (mail: PO Box 192)912.449.2026Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
Board of Assessors312 Nichols Street, Blackshear, GA 31516 (mail: PO Box 589)912.449.2025Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The commissioner takes property tax payments online, and they post on the next business day. Cards other than American Express are accepted with a convenience fee. A Georgia driver's license with a Pierce County address is required to title or tag a vehicle in the county.

Three authorities set millage: the county commissioners, the school board and the State. Which rate applies to you depends on whether the parcel lies in Blackshear, Patterson or unincorporated land, so ask the commissioner which millage is on your bill. The county's millage page links the current digest with its five-year levy history, and it is worth a look before you price the house. Ask too whether any rate change is pending, since a buyer's lender will use the current bill to estimate the monthly payment.

sections.h2: Due date and how to pay
sections.html:
Your bill carries the due date, and the commissioner's office can confirm it by phone. December 20 is the official state date, yet a county can pass a resolution for December 1 or November 15, or split billing into installments.

A few rules help sellers:

  • Interest waits 60 days after the bill is postmarked, and penalties can follow if the balance goes delinquent.
  • Pierce County property is taxed to the owner as of January 1.
  • The return window at the county tax office runs January 1 to April 1.
  • A manufactured home parked in Pierce on January 1 gets its return and its location permit on the same visit, before April 1.

Before you visit either office, have your parcel number, a photo ID and your deed handy. If you are filing a return on a manufactured home, bring the home's details as well so the location permit can be issued during the same trip. Calling ahead on 912.449.2025 for the assessors or 912.449.2026 for the commissioner saves a wasted drive in a county where distances are long.

The commissioner's site also lists a tax sale registration form and an excess funds list. If your parcel is behind on payments, call 912.449.2026 before you list so you know how much to pay off at closing.

After the assessors set a new value, a notice goes to the taxpayer, who has 45 days to appeal in writing. Late appeals are invalid. An appeal may rest on taxability, uniformity or value.

The appeal runs in stages:

  • The Board of Assessors reviews the appeal first and decides whether a change is warranted.
  • If the value stands, the Grand Jury's appointees on the three-person Board of Equalization hear the dispute next.
  • Either side may take the decision to Pierce County Superior Court.

Appraisers work from three methods: cost, comparable sales and income. Field staff may stop at a parcel to look into an appeal, a return, a new addition or a conservation application. Visitors from the office show photo identification and arrive in a marked county vehicle. To meet with the Board of Assessors, book by the Friday before its 9:00 a.m. session; the board sits at least twice monthly.

The homestead exemption is available at the assessors' office year-round, but it must be filed by April 1 to reduce the current year's bill. A purchase made after New Year's Day misses that year's exemption, since the January 1 test looks at who owned and lived there. Once granted, it stays in place until you move or the ownership changes. The county offers no local homestead exemptions, so state exemptions are what applies. Ask the assessors what your age or veteran status adds.

Special programs can lower the value of land:

  • Preferential farmland is assessed at 30 percent instead of 40, and the owner commits to ten years of farm use.
  • Conservation use assessment values bona fide farm and forest land at current use value.
  • Environmentally sensitive property and residential transitional property can also use current use value.
  • Trees on the stump escape tax until they are sold or cut, then count at full market value.

Land held under a covenant deserves a question to the assessors, before the contract is signed, about how a sale or a new use changes things. Farm and timber parcels are a real part of sales here, and the covenant terms are worth requesting in writing.

Call the commissioner at 912.449.2026 for a written balance, including any interest or penalty, and hand it to the closing attorney. The year's tax is owed by the January 1 owner, so the sale contract decides how it is split with the buyer. Anything unpaid comes out of your proceeds at closing.

A cash sale skips the lender's review and an appraisal wait, which can help when a bill is behind or the house needs repairs a lender might question. The buyer files a fresh homestead application, and the April 1 date still applies to them. Ask the assessors for the covenant papers if the land is enrolled in a farm or forest program.

If the account is far behind, the commissioner's tax sale page and excess funds list show how delinquent parcels are handled, which is a good reason to settle the balance before a sale rather than after.

faqs.q: Where is the Pierce County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: It is at 312 Nichols Street, Suite 4, in Blackshear, Georgia, with hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone is 912.449.2026.

faqs.q: What is the Pierce County property tax due date?
faqs.a: Check your bill or ask the commissioner. December 20 is the state's default, which a county can replace with an earlier date or installments.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for a Pierce County assessment?
faqs.a: Written appeals must arrive inside 45 days of the notice date. Any later appeal is invalid.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pierce County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner accepts major cards except American Express, with a convenience fee, and online payments post on the next business day.

faqs.q: When must a Pierce County homestead exemption be filed?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year you want it. Ownership and residence on January 1 of that year are both required.
